message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"9.15","text":"For just as formidable snakes draw sparrows toward themselves with their breaths, so these demons also draw those who partake of their table into their own will, having mixed themselves into their minds through the food and drink. They transform themselves in dreams according to the likenesses of the carved images in order to increase the deception. For the carved image is neither a living creature nor does it possess a divine spirit; rather, the demon that was seen made use of its form. To how many others have they similarly appeared in dreams, and did those people not agree when they met one another while awake and compared what was in the dream? Consequently, what might appear is no longer a dream; rather, it either belongs to a demon or consists of the products of a soul that assigns the forms to the παρίᾳ fears and to desire. For, alternatively, when its mind has been struck by fear, it gives birth to the forms through dreams. But if you think that the carved images, since they are animate, can perform such things, set them on a balance when its beam is level, place the counterweight on the other pan, and call upon them to become either heavier or lighter. If that happens, they are animate; but it does not happen. If, however, it should happen, such a thing is in that way a god. For even this can happen by the finger of a demon. Worms also move, and they are not called gods.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οἱ δεινοὶ ὄφεις τοῖς αὐτῶν πνεύμασιν τοὺς στρουθοὺς ἐπισπῶνται","chosen":"formidable snakes draw sparrows toward themselves with their breaths","rationale":"πνεύματα here are the snakes’ breaths or exhalations, and στρουθοί most naturally denotes sparrows or small birds."},{"source_quote":"διά γε τῶν βρωτῶν καὶ ποτῶν ἀνακραθέντες αὐτῶν τῷ νῷ","chosen":"having mixed themselves into their minds through the food and drink","rationale":"ἀνακραθέντες portrays the demons as becoming mixed with the participants’ mind by means of what is eaten and drunk."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὰς τῶν ξοάνων ἰδέας","chosen":"according to the likenesses of the carved images","rationale":"ξόανον is a carved cult image, often wooden, while ἰδέαι here are its visible forms or likenesses."},{"source_quote":"πόσοις κατ’ ὄναρ ὁμοίως ἄλλοις ὤφθησαν καὶ ὕπαρ συναντήσαντες ἀλλήλοις πρὸς τὸ κατ’ ὄναρ ἀντιβάλλοντες οὐ συνεφώνησαν;","chosen":"To how many others have they similarly appeared in dreams, and did those people not agree when they met one another while awake and compared what was in the dream?","rationale":"The rendering takes πόσοις ... ἄλλοις together as “to how many others,” while the following participles refer contextually to the people comparing their dream experiences. Another possible attachment takes ὁμοίως ἄλλοις as “like other people.” The negative οὐ συνεφώνησαν is retained as “did ... not agree.”"},{"source_quote":"ὕπαρ συναντήσαντες ἀλλήλοις","chosen":"when they met one another while awake","rationale":"ὕπαρ contrasts waking experience with what was experienced in a dream."},{"source_quote":"ὥστε οὐκέτι ὄναρ ἐπιφανείη ἐκεῖνό ἐστιν","chosen":"Consequently, what might appear is no longer a dream","rationale":"The rendering takes ἐκεῖνο as the subject associated with optative ἐπιφανείη and ὄναρ as the predicate of ἐστιν. The construction is irregular; alternatively, ὄναρ may be adverbial, yielding the sense that what appears in a dream is not the thing whose form it bears."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς παρίᾳ φόβοις καὶ ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἀποδιδούσης τὰς ἰδέας","chosen":"that assigns the forms to the παρίᾳ fears and to desire","rationale":"The exact printed παρίᾳ is retained untranslated because no defensible lexical and syntactic account has been established for it in this construction. The surrounding datives support “to the ... fears and to desire,” but παρίᾳ does not straightforwardly agree with plural φόβοις, and rendering it from the word for “cheek” would not establish a coherent relation."},{"source_quote":"ἢ γὰρ φόβῳ τὸν νοῦν πληγεῖσα","chosen":"For, alternatively, when its mind has been struck by fear","rationale":"“For” represents γάρ and “alternatively” represents the printed disjunctive ἢ without silently adopting the conjectural replacement ἡ."},{"source_quote":"διὰ ὀνείρων τὰς ἰδέας ἀποκυΐσκει","chosen":"it gives birth to the forms through dreams","rationale":"ἀποκυΐσκω uses the image of conceiving or giving birth, here applied to the soul’s production of dream forms."},{"source_quote":"εἰ δὲ ἔσται, οὕτω τὸ τοιοῦτο θεός ἐστιν","chosen":"If, however, it should happen, such a thing is in that way a god","rationale":"The selected text and punctuation present this as a statement. The surrounding reductio could support hearing it rhetorically as “is such a thing therefore a god?”, but that punctuation is not imposed on the main text."},{"source_quote":"δακτύλῳ δαίμονος","chosen":"by the finger of a demon","rationale":"The rendering retains the concrete image of a demon’s finger as the means by which the apparent change could be produced."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὥστε οὐκέτι ὄναρ ἐπιφανείη ἐκεῖνό ἐστιν","issue":"The relation of optative ἐπιφανείη, neuter ἐκεῖνο, ὄναρ, and ἐστιν is syntactically irregular. The main rendering treats ὄναρ as the predicate and ἐκεῖνο as what might appear. A contextually plausible alternative takes ὄναρ adverbially and understands the clause as saying that what appears in a dream is not the actual thing whose form it bears. Both analyses require some accommodation of the compressed construction.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τοῖς παρίᾳ φόβοις καὶ ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἀποδιδούσης τὰς ἰδέας","issue":"The image-verified selected edition reads παρίᾳ. The form does not straightforwardly agree with plural φόβοις, and no defensible contextual meaning or alternative syntactic attachment for the exact printed word has been established. Identifying it with a word for “cheek” does not by itself yield a supported rendering. No evidenced textual correction is adopted, so the main text retains παρίᾳ untranslated. Because surviving Greek wording remains without a defensible English rendering, publication is blocked.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"ἢ γὰρ φόβῳ τὸν νοῦν πληγεῖσα","issue":"The printed ἢ is retained in the main text as a disjunctive represented by “alternatively,” with γάρ represented by “For.” The conjecture ἡ would instead make the feminine article directly introduce πληγεῖσα and yield, “For the soul, when struck in its mind by fear,” but that conjecture is not adopted as the supplied reading.","proposed_reading":"ἡ γὰρ φόβῳ τὸν νοῦν πληγεῖσα","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
